questions.question: The intense rainfall on the western side of the Western Ghats is due to which type of rainfall mechanism?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Orographic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The** intense rainfall** on the **western side **of the **Western Ghats **is caused by the **orographic rainfall mechanism**.
 
• Orographic rainfall occurs when moist air is forced to rise over a mountain range, leading to **cooling, condensation, and precipitation**.
 
• The Western Ghats act as a **natural barrier**, causing the moisture-laden southwest monsoon winds to rise and result in heavy rainfall on the windward side.
 
• The **windward side** of the Western Ghats receives significantly **higher rainfall**, while the **leeward side **remains relatively dry, creating a **rain shadow region**.
 
• This phenomenon is common in regions with prominent mountain ranges, particularly in tropical and subtropical climates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Orographic Rainfall:**

 
 
• This type of rainfall is also known as **relief rainfall**.
 
• It occurs when air masses are forced to rise due to the presence of a mountain or elevated terrain.
 
• As the air rises, it cools and its capacity to hold moisture decreases, leading to condensation and precipitation.
 
 
 
• **Windward vs. Leeward Side:**
 
 
• The windward side faces the incoming moist winds and receives heavy rainfall.
 
• The leeward side, sheltered from the winds, remains dry and is termed as the **rain shadow region**.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Western Ghats:**
 
 
• The Western Ghats are recognized as a biodiversity hotspot and are crucial for India's monsoon dynamics.
 
• The region supports agriculture, hydropower generation, and water supply for surrounding areas.
 
 
 
• **Other Types of Rainfall:**
 
 
• **Convectional Rainfall:** Caused by the heating of the Earth's surface, common in equatorial regions.
 
• **Cyclonic Rainfall:** Associated with cyclones and low-pressure systems.
 
• **Frontal Rainfall:** Occurs when warm and cold air masses meet, leading to precipitation along the front.

questions.question: Daksh travels 445 km at 89 km/hr, the next 495 km at 55 km/hr and the next 250 km at 50 km/hr. What is his average speed (in km/hr) for the whole journey? (Corrected to two decimal places)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Average Speed** = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time 1 = 445 ÷ 89 = 5 hours

Time 2 = 495 ÷ 55 = 9 hours

Time 3 = 250 ÷ 50 = 5 hours

Average Speed = (445 + 495 + 250) ÷ (5 + 9 + 5) = 1190 ÷ 19 = 62.63 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 62.63 km/hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aa71243a8a1d34a3a15f73b978ea21c435d85ac37ef716039d58c41be8dbf39b.png] 

**Given:**

Distances: **d₁** = 445 km, **d₂** = 495 km, **d₃** = 250 km

Speeds: **s₁** = 89 km/hr, **s₂** = 55 km/hr, **s₃** = 50 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

**Time (t)** = Distance (d) ÷ Speed (s)

**Average Speed** = (d₁ + d₂ + d₃) ÷ (t₁ + t₂ + t₃)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 445 + 495 + 250 = 1190 km

⇒ t₁ = 445 ÷ 89 = 5 hours

⇒ t₂ = 495 ÷ 55 = 9 hours

⇒ t₃ = 250 ÷ 50 = 5 hours

⇒ Total Time = 5 + 9 + 5 = 19 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 1190 ÷ 19

⇒ Average Speed ≈ 62.6315...

**∴ The correct answer is 62.63 km/hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distances

If two equal distances are covered at speeds u and v, Average Speed = (2 × u × v) ÷ (u + v).

Relative Speed

In the same direction, speed = S₁ − S₂. In opposite directions, speed = S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: Which of the following statements accurately describes the behavior of continuing numbering from a previous list when inserting a new numbered list within the same document in MS Word?

MS Word automatically restarts the numbering from 1 for the new list, and there is no direct way to continue the previous sequence.

• If the numbering style or level of the new list matches the previous list, the continuation option can be applied seamlessly.
 
• Restarting numbering is the default behavior unless the "Continue from previous list" option is selected.
 
• This feature is particularly useful when working with multi-level lists or documents requiring consistent numbering across sections.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Restarting vs. Continuing Numbering:**

questions.question: Find the value of (K² - 5) , if the quadratic equation 2x² - 8x + K = 0 has real and equal roots.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For a quadratic equation to have **equal roots**, the constant term K must satisfy K = b² / 4a.

Here, a = 2 and b = −8.

K = (−8)² / (4 × 2) = 64 / 8 = 8.

The required value is K² − 5 = 8² − 5 = 64 − 5 = 59.

**∴ The correct answer is 59.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The quadratic equation is 2x² − 8x + K = 0.

**Formula Used:** A quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0 has **real and equal roots** if its **Discriminant (D)** is zero, i.e., D = b² − 4ac = 0.

Comparing 2x² − 8x + K = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0:

⇒ a = 2, b = −8, c = K

⇒ D = (−8)² − 4 × 2 × K = 0

⇒ 64 − 8K = 0

⇒ 8K = 64

⇒ K = 64 ÷ 8 = 8

Now, we need to find the value of (K² − 5):

⇒ K² − 5 = 8² − 5

⇒ 64 − 5 = 59

**∴ The correct answer is 59.**

**__Additional Information__**

Nature of Roots

The nature of roots depends on D = b² − 4ac. If D > 0, roots are real and distinct; if D = 0, roots are real and equal; if D < 0, roots are imaginary.

Sum and Product of Roots

For ax² + bx + c = 0, the sum of roots (α + β) = −b/a and the product of roots (αβ) = c/a.

Quadratic Formula

The roots of a quadratic equation are given by x = (−b ± √D) / 2a.</p

questions.question: The average of 9 numbers is 17. The average of 7 of these numbers is 16. The average of the remaining two numbers is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Base **Average** of 9 numbers = 17.

Deviation of 7 numbers from the average = 16 − 17 = −1.

Total deviation to be balanced by the **remaining two** numbers = − (7 × (−1)) = +7.

Average of remaining two numbers = 17 + (7 ÷ 2) = 17 + 3.5 = 20.5.

**∴ The correct answer is 20.5.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average of **9 numbers** = 17

Average of **7 numbers** = 16

**Formula Used:**

Sum = Average × Number of items

Average of remaining items = (Total Sum − Sum of known items) ÷ Remaining items count

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ef4359b60d4be07114662da32612a19faa2d1703e0b11adb8f3a2de15b7d7e72.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of 9 numbers = 9 × 17 = 153

⇒ Sum of 7 numbers = 7 × 16 = 112

⇒ Sum of **remaining two** numbers = 153 − 112 = 41

⇒ Average of remaining two numbers = 41 ÷ 2 = 20.5

**∴ The correct answer is 20.5.**

**__Additional Information__**

Net Deviation Rule

The algebraic sum of the deviations of all observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero. This is used to find missing values or averages quickly.

Weighted Average

When two groups with averages A₁ and A₂ and sizes n₁ and n₂ are combined, the new average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Arithmetic Mean Formula

Average = Total Sum of Observations ÷ Total Number of Observations.</p

questions.question: Which Harappan site shows evidence of ploughed fields?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalibangan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kalibangan** is a prominent Harappan site located in present-day Rajasthan, India.
 
• It is unique among Harappan sites for providing evidence of **ploughed agricultural fields**.
 
• The ploughed field marks at Kalibangan are indicative of early agricultural practices in the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• These field impressions were discovered near the southern part of the site, showing **furrows aligned in two directions**, suggesting advanced farming techniques.
 
• The discovery highlights the significance of agriculture in the economy of the Harappan civilization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indus Valley Civilization**:

 
 
• It is one of the world's earliest urban civilizations, dating back to** 2500 BCE**.
 
• Major sites include **Mohenjo-daro, Harappa, Dholavira, Lothal, and Kalibangan**.
 
• Known for advanced town planning, drainage systems, and standardized weights and measures.
 
 
 
• **Kalibangan’s Historical Significance**:
 
 
• Kalibangan is divided into two parts: the **citadel **(western mound) and the **lower town** (eastern mound).
 
• The site shows evidence of fire altars, indicating ritualistic practices.
 
• It also provides evidence of mud-brick structures typical of Harappan architecture.
 
 
 
• **Ploughed Fields in Archaeology**:
 
 
• Ploughed field impressions are rare in archaeology and provide insights into ancient agricultural practices.
 
• Such discoveries help reconstruct the methods of crop cultivation used by early civilizations.
 
 
 
• **Agriculture in the Harappan Civilization**:
 
 
• Major crops included **wheat, barley, sesame, mustard, and cotton**.
 
• Advanced irrigation techniques and seasonal cultivation were practiced.
 
• Kalibangan’s evidence of ploughed fields complements the broader understanding of Harappan agriculture.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT the use of baking soda in the kitchen?

• Baking soda is utilized in **fire extinguishers**, especially for kitchen fires, as it releases carbon dioxide to smother flames.
 
• Baking soda **does not serve as a food coloring agent**; its chemical properties are not designed for altering the color of food.

• **Fire Extinguishing Use:** Baking soda releases carbon dioxide when heated, which helps extinguish small grease fires by cutting off the oxygen supply.
 
• **Other Household Uses:** Baking soda is widely used for cleaning, deodorizing, and personal care, such as teeth whitening and skin exfoliation.

⇒ 48 − __**8 ÷ 56**__ × 24 + 6

⇒ __**(336 − 24)/7**__ + 6

**4) 48 W 8 Z 56 Y 24 X 6**

⇒ __**48 ÷ 8**__ − 56 + 24 × 6

⇒ 6 − 56 + __**24 × 6**__

⇒ __**6 − 56**__ + 144

⇒ __**−50 + 144**__

⇒ 94

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

questions.question: In most Unix-based operating systems, which command is used to create an empty file if the file does not already exist?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**touch**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **touch** command in Unix-based operating systems is used to create an empty file if the file does not already exist.
 
• If the file exists, the **touch** command updates the file's timestamp, which includes access and modification times.
 
• Syntax for the command: touch filename. Replace filename with the desired name of the file.
 
• **Touch** does not modify the content of the file; it only creates or updates metadata such as timestamps.
 
• This command is particularly useful for scripting and testing purposes where files need to be generated without content.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **mkdir:**

 
 
• Used to create directories, not files.
 
• Syntax: mkdir directory_name.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the components of the Panchayati Raj institutions in India at the village level?

__
 
• The Panchayati Raj system in India is a three-tier structure consisting of the Gram Panchayat at the village level, the Panchayat Samiti at the block level, and the Zila Parishad at the district level.
 
• **The Panchayat Samiti does not operate at the village level**. It functions at the block level, acting as an intermediary body between the Gram Panchayat and the Zila Parishad.
 
• The components of the Panchayati Raj system at the village level include the Gram Sabha, Gram Panchayat, and Nyaya Panchayat.
 
• The Gram Sabha is the general assembly of all the registered voters in a village, while the Gram Panchayat is the executive body responsible for governance and development activities.
 
• The Nyaya Panchayat, where established, handles minor disputes and judicial matters at the village level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gram Sabha:**

 
 
• The Gram Sabha is the foundational body of the Panchayati Raj system, consisting of all the registered voters in a village.
 
• It plays a key role in decision-making, approving budgets, and monitoring the functioning of the Gram Panchayat.
 
 
 
• **Gram Panchayat:**
 
 
• The Gram Panchayat is the executive body of the village-level Panchayati Raj system.
 
• It is responsible for implementing development programs, maintaining public infrastructure, and ensuring welfare schemes reach the beneficiaries.
 
 
 
• **Nyaya Panchayat:**
 
 
• Nyaya Panchayats are quasi-judicial bodies established at the village level in some states to handle minor civil and criminal disputes.
 
• They aim to provide accessible and speedy justice to rural citizens without the need for formal legal proceedings.
 
 
 
• **Panchayat Samiti:**
 
 
• The Panchayat Samiti operates at the block level, coordinating and supervising the activities of the Gram Panchayats under its jurisdiction.
 
• It is responsible for planning and implementing development programs at the block level.
 
 
 
• **Zila Parishad:**
 
 
• The Zila Parishad is the apex body of the Panchayati Raj system, functioning at the district level.
 
• It coordinates development activities and provides administrative support to the Panchayat Samitis and Gram Panchayats.

questions.question: Which of the following agricultural practices is called Ponam in Kerala and Podu in Odisha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shifting Cultivation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Shifting cultivation** is known as **Ponam in Kerala and Podu in Odisha**, reflecting regional nomenclature for this agricultural practice.
 
• It involves** clearing forests through slash-and-burn methods**, cultivating crops temporarily, and then shifting to another area once soil fertility declines.
 
• This method is widely practiced by tribal communities in hilly and forested regions of India, including Odisha, Kerala, and the North-Eastern states.
 
• It is considered a traditional form of agriculture that supports subsistence farming for communities dependent on forest resources.
 
• Though it provides temporary agricultural productivity, shifting cultivation is often criticized for contributing to deforestation and soil erosion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Slash-and-Burn Agriculture:** This method involves cutting vegetation and burning it to clear land for cultivation. The ash acts as a nutrient source for the soil.
 
• **Subsistence Farming:** A type of farming where farmers grow crops primarily for their family's consumption, with little to no surplus for trade.
 
• **Impact on Environment:** Shifting cultivation can lead to loss of biodiversity, deforestation, soil degradation, and disruption of local ecosystems.
 
• **Alternative Practices:** Governments and organizations encourage sustainable agricultural practices like agroforestry and terraced farming to replace shifting cultivation.
 
• **Regions Practicing Shifting Cultivation:** Besides India, this method is practiced globally in tropical regions such as Southeast Asia, Africa, and South America.

questions.question: The curved surface area of a cylinder is half of its total surface area. If its height is 102 cm, then find its radius (in cm).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If **Curved Surface Area (CSA)** is half of **Total Surface Area (TSA)**, then **CSA = TSA ÷ 2**.

This condition 2×**CSA** = **TSA** simplifies to 2×(2πrh) = 2πr(h + r).

Further simplification: 2h = h + r ⇒ **h = r**.

Since **height (h)** is 102 cm, the **radius (r)** must also be 102 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 102 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Height (h)** of the cylinder = 102 cm

**Condition:** CSA = 1/2 × TSA

**Formula Used:**

**Curved Surface Area (CSA)** = 2πrh

**Total Surface Area (TSA)** = 2πr(h + r)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/77dded3777171208b30142eda7cf20b958eda5eacaec742fe3cb9593cc5b001c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2πrh = 1/2 × [2πr(h + r)]

⇒ 2πrh = πr(h + r)

⇒ 2h = h + r (By cancelling πr on both sides)

⇒ 2h − h = r

⇒ r = h

⇒ r = 102 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 102 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of Cylinder

The **volume** of a cylinder is the product of base area and height, given by V = πr²h.

Relationship between CSA and TSA

**Total Surface Area** is the sum of **Curved Surface Area** and the area of the two circular bases: TSA = CSA + 2×(πr²).

Hollow Cylinder

For a **hollow cylinder** with outer radius R and inner radius r, the Volume = π(R² − r²)h.</p

questions.question: Train A running at a speed of 72 km/hr takes 24 seconds to completely cross train B running at 63 km/hr in the opposite direction. The length of train B is 1.5 times the length of train A. Train B crosses a bridge completely in 62 seconds. The length of the bridge (in m) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Speed** in opposite direction = 72 + 63 = 135 kmph = 135 × (5/18) = 37.5 m/s.

Total distance (LA + LB) = Speed × Time = 37.5 × 24 = 900 m.

Given LB = 1.5 LA ⇒ LA + 1.5 LA = 900 ⇒ 2.5 LA = 900 ⇒ LA = 360 m, LB = 540 m.

Speed of Train B = 63 × (5/18) = 17.5 m/s.

Bridge Length = (SpeedB × Time) − LB = (17.5 × 62) − 540 = 1085 − 540 = 545 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 545 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a179c27f4d1815a86fec149dba4031504195d46d118c9265efba4aeb112b7ffd.png] 

**Step 1: Find lengths of trains.**

⇒ SpeedA = 72 × 5/18 = 20 m/s; SpeedB = 63 × 5/18 = 17.5 m/s.

⇒ Relative Speed = 20 + 17.5 = 37.5 m/s.

⇒ Sum of lengths (LA + LB) = 37.5 × 24 = 900 m.

⇒ LA + 1.5 LA = 900 ⇒ 2.5 LA = 900 ⇒ LA = 360 m.

⇒ LB = 1.5 × 360 = 540 m.

**Step 2: Find bridge length.**

⇒ Total Distance = SpeedB × Time = 17.5 × 62 = 1085 m.

⇒ Bridge Length = Total Distance − LB = 1085 − 540 = 545 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 545 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in **opposite directions**, their relative speed is the **sum** of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). In the same direction, it is the **difference** (|S₁ − S₂|).

Crossing Distance Rule

When a train crosses another train or a bridge, the **total distance** covered is always the **sum of the lengths** of the train and the object being crossed.

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/hr to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: Independent dance numbers such as Chali, Ramdani and Jhumura are associated with which of the following dance forms?

__
 
• **Sattriya** is a classical dance form of India, originating from **Assam **and was introduced in the **15th century by the Vaishnavite saint Srimanta Sankardev**.
 
• It combines **music, dance, and drama** and is deeply rooted in Vaishnavism, reflecting devotion to Lord Krishna.
 
• Independent dance numbers such as **Chali, Ramdani, and Jhumura** are integral parts of the Sattriya repertoire.
 
• Sattriya was traditionally performed in **satras (monasteries)** by male monks as part of religious rituals and teachings.
 
• In 2000, Sattriya was recognized as one of the **eight classical dance forms of India** by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Classical Dance Forms of India:**

 
 
• India has eight officially recognized classical dance forms: **Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Kuchipudi, and Sattriya**.
 
• These dances are characterized by their distinct styles and are deeply rooted in spiritual and cultural traditions.
 
 
 
• **Sattras:**
 
 
• Sattras are Vaishnavite monasteries established by Srimanta Sankardev in Assam.
 
• They served as centers for spiritual learning, art, music, and dance.
 
 
 
• **Key Components of Sattriya:**
 
 
• Sattriya consists of Ankiya Nat (drama), Borgeet (devotional songs), and distinct dance numbers like Chali and Jhumura.
 
• It uses intricate hand gestures (mudras), rhythmic footwork, and expressive facial movements.
 
 
 
• **Recognition by Sangeet Natak Akademi:**

questions.question: Why does the parliamentary system prevent executive despotism?

options.text: Because the Prime Minister has unlimited power
Because the judiciary can override executive decisions without checks
Because executive authority is dispersed among a group of ministers accountable to the Parliament
Because the military can intervene in governance

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Because executive authority is dispersed among a group of ministers accountable to the Parliament**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **parliamentary system ensures that the executive authority is not concentrated in one individual** but is collectively shared by a cabinet of ministers.
 
• Ministers in the executive are accountable to the Parliament, which acts as a check against any form of authoritarianism or unilateral decision-making.
 
• The **Prime Minister and cabinet members can be questioned, censured, or removed** through parliamentary mechanisms such as votes of no confidence.
 
• This system promotes transparency and prevents the abuse of executive power by subjecting it to parliamentary oversight and democratic processes.
 
• The dispersal of power among various ministers prevents despotism and ensures collective decision-making aligned with public interests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parliamentary Democracy:**

 
 
• A system of government where the executive branch derives its legitimacy from the legislative branch and is accountable to it.
 
• Examples include the UK, India, and Canada.
 
 
 
• **Vote of No Confidence:**
 
 
• A parliamentary procedure used to remove a government or executive by showing that it no longer has the majority support of the legislature.
 
• It is an essential tool to ensure executive accountability in a parliamentary system.
 
 
 
• **Separation of Powers:**
 
 
• A principle where governmental powers are divided among different branches: executive, legislative, and judiciary.
 
• In a parliamentary system, the executive and legislature are closely linked, unlike in a presidential system where they are separate.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Oversight:**
 
 
• The judiciary in parliamentary democracies can review executive actions to ensure compliance with the Constitution.
 
• This further prevents authoritarian tendencies in governance.
 
 
 
• **Collective Responsibility:**
 
 
• A principle in parliamentary systems where all cabinet members share responsibility for decisions and policies of the government.
 
• This ensures accountability and prevents individual despotism within the executive.

questions.question: In glycolysis, which enzyme catalyses the rate-limiting phosphorylation of fructose-6 phosphate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phosphofructokinase-1 (PFK-1)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Phosphofructokinase-1 (PFK-1)** is the **rate-limiting enzyme** in glycolysis, catalyzing the phosphorylation of fructose-6-phosphate to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate.
 
• PFK-1 is an allosteric enzyme regulated by ATP, citrate, and AMP, ensuring glycolysis responds to the cell's energy needs.
 
• This enzyme plays a critical role in controlling the flux of glucose metabolism under different physiological conditions.
 
• High levels of ATP inhibit PFK-1 activity, while AMP and fructose-2,6-bisphosphate activate it, ensuring energy production aligns with cellular demands.
 
• PFK-1 is active in the cytoplasm and is essential for anaerobic and aerobic energy production pathways.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Glycolysis**

 
 
• Glycolysis is a **10-step metabolic pathway that converts glucose into pyruvate**, generating ATP and NADH.
 
• It occurs in the cytoplasm of cells and is the first stage of cellular respiration.
 
• The pathway can function under both aerobic and anaerobic conditions.
 
• The primary products of glycolysis are 2 molecules of pyruvate, 2 ATP, and 2 NADH per glucose molecule.
 
 
 
• **Hexokinase**
 
 
• Hexokinase catalyzes the first step of glycolysis, converting glucose to glucose-6-phosphate.
 
• It is inhibited by its product, glucose-6-phosphate, to regulate glucose uptake.
 
 
 
• **Pyruvate Kinase**
 
 
• Pyruvate kinase catalyzes the final step of glycolysis, converting phosphoenolpyruvate to pyruvate.
 
• It is regulated by fructose-1,6-bisphosphate (feed-forward activation) and ATP (inhibition).
 
 
 
• **Fructose-2,6-bisphosphate**
 
 
• This molecule is a potent activator of PFK-1, enhancing glycolysis during high energy demand.
 
• Fructose-2,6-bisphosphate is synthesized by phosphofructokinase-2 (PFK-2) in response to hormonal signals like insulin.

questions.question: Find the area of a sector with a central angle of 150° in a circle with a radius of 12 cm.

The total boundary of the sector includes the arc and two radii: Perimeter = l + 2r.</p

questions.question: In which of the following cases did the court restrict the Parliament from curtailing any Fundamental Right?

options.text: Kesavananda Bharati vs State of Kerala
A K Gopalan vs State of Madras

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Golaknath vs State of Punjab**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **In Golaknath vs State of Punjab**, the Supreme Court ruled that Parliament cannot curtail or amend Fundamental Rights under the Constitution.
 
• The court held that Fundamental Rights are transcendental and cannot be abridged by ordinary legislation.
 
• This judgment restricted Parliament’s power to amend Fundamental Rights under Article 368.
 
• **Later,** in the **Kesavananda Bharati case (1973)**, Parliament was allowed to amend the Constitution but not in a way that destroys its basic structure, including Fundamental Rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Basic Structure Doctrine:**

 
 
• Introduced in the Kesavananda Bharati case, it holds that certain fundamental features of the Constitution cannot be altered or destroyed through amendments.
 
• Examples of such features include the supremacy of the Constitution, secularism, democracy, and judicial independence.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights:**
 
 
• These are enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution and guarantee civil liberties such as equality, freedom, and protection against exploitation.
 
• They ensure that Indian citizens can live with dignity and freedom within the framework of the law.
 
 
 
• **24th Constitutional Amendment:**
 
 
• Passed in 1971, it empowered Parliament to amend any part of the Constitution, including Fundamental Rights.
 
• This amendment was challenged in the Kesavananda Bharati case.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Review:**
 
 
• This refers to the power of the judiciary to examine the constitutionality of legislative and executive actions.
 
• It was reaffirmed in the Kesavananda Bharati case as a feature of the Basic Structure.
 
 
 
• **Golaknath vs State of Punjab (1967):**
 
 
• In this case, the Supreme Court ruled that Parliament could not amend Fundamental Rights.
 
• This decision was later modified by the Kesavananda Bharati judgment, which allowed amendments but restricted them under the Basic Structure Doctrine.

questions.question: Two numbers are respectively 46% and 54% more than a third number. The ratio of the two numbers is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume the **third number** is 100.

**First number** = 100 + 46 = 146

**Second number** = 100 + 54 = 154

Ratio = 146 : 154 = 73 : 77

**∴ The correct answer is 73 : 77.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a2c519ad4e384fcb96ed0e643a70e0886cf42c901fba047e5b7c0bd385ecaa6.png] 

**Given:**

Let the **third number** be x.

⇒ **First number** = x + 46% of x = 1.46x

⇒ **Second number** = x + 54% of x = 1.54x

**Calculation:**

⇒ Required Ratio = First number : Second number

⇒ Ratio = 1.46x : 1.54x

⇒ Ratio = 146 : 154

⇒ Ratio = (146 ÷ 2) : (154 ÷ 2)

⇒ Ratio = 73 : 77

**∴ The correct answer is 73 : 77.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Increase

If a value is increased by k%, the new value is (1 + k/100) × Original Value.

Ratio Simplification

To simplify a ratio a : b, divide both terms by their **Highest Common Factor (HCF)**.

Base Value Selection

In comparison problems, it is usually easiest to assume the **base reference number** (third number) as 100.</p

Let us arrange the data in ascending order to count the frequencies systematically:

40, 41, 41, 41, 44, 45, 46, 47, 47, 48, 48, 49, 50, 53, 53, 54, 54, 55

⇒ Frequency of 40 = 1

⇒ Frequency of 44 = 1

⇒ Frequency of 45 = 1

⇒ Frequency of 46 = 1

⇒ Frequency of 47 = 2

⇒ Frequency of 48 = 2

⇒ Frequency of 50 = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 41.**

**__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship is given by: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Types of Mode Distributions

A dataset can have one mode (unimodal), two modes (bimodal), three modes (trimodal), or no mode if all values occur with the same frequency.

Median of a Dataset

The middle value when the data is arranged in ascending or descending order. For N terms, if N is odd, Median = ((N+1)/2)th term; if N is even, Median = Average of (N/2)th and (N/2 + 1)th terms.</p

questions.question: In the reaction: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, if 5 moles of H₂ and 2 moles of O₂ are mixed, the limiting reagent is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**O₂**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In a chemical reaction, the **limiting reagent is the reactant that is completely consumed first, limiting the amount of product formed**.
 
• The reaction provided is **2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O**, where 2 moles of H₂ react with 1 mole of O₂ to form 2 moles of water (H₂O).
 
• Given 5 moles of H₂ and 2 moles of O₂, the stoichiometric ratio is analyzed: 5 moles H₂ would require (5/2) = 2.5 moles of O₂, but only 2 moles of O₂ are available.
 
• Since O₂ is insufficient to react with all the H₂, it is the limiting reagent.
 
• The excess reactant in this scenario is H₂, as not all 5 moles of H₂ can react due to the shortage of O₂.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Limiting Reagent:**

 
 
• The reactant that determines the maximum amount of product formed in a chemical reaction.
 
• It is completely consumed during the reaction, leaving other reactants in excess.
 
 
 
• **Stoichiometry:**
 
 
• The quantitative relationship between reactants and products in a balanced chemical equation.
 
• It helps in determining the mole ratio required for a reaction.
 
 
 
• **Mole Concept:**
 
 
• A mole represents 6.022 × 10²³ particles (Avogadro's number) of a substance.
 
• Moles are used to express quantities in chemical reactions for easy stoichiometric calculations.
 
 
 
• **Excess Reagent:**
 
 
• The reactant that remains unreacted after the limiting reagent is completely consumed.
 
• In this case, H₂ is the excess reagent.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Limiting Reagent Concept:**
 
 
• Used in industrial chemical processes to optimize reactant usage.
 
• Helps prevent wastage and reduce costs by determining the exact proportions of reactants.

questions.question: A bank offers 7.8% compound interest per annum calculated on a half-yearly basis. A customer deposits ₹9,920 each on 1 January and 1 July of a year. At the end of the year, the amount he would have gained by way of interest is ______ (give your answer correct to 2 decimal places).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Half-yearly rate** (r) = 7.8% ÷ 2 = 3.9%.

**Effective rate** for 1st deposit (2 periods) = 3.9 + 3.9 + (3.9 × 3.9)/100 = 7.9521%.

**Effective rate** for 2nd deposit (1 period) = 3.9%.

**Total Interest %** = 7.9521% + 3.9% = 11.8521%.

**Interest gained** = 9920 × 11.8521 ÷ 100 ≈ ₹1,175.73.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,175.73.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Principal (P)** = ₹9,920 each on **1 January** and **1 July**.

**Annual Rate (R)** = 7.8% | **Half-yearly rate (r)** = 7.8% ÷ 2 = 3.9%.

**Time:** End of the year (31 December).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e4960c9e9cb6a3440da3218848ffff004bb36d9db1a4f87c20d0f4bb860d82a.png]

**Step 2: Interest on this amount for the next 6 months:**

⇒ I₂ = 10306.88 × (3.9 ÷ 100) = ₹401.96832

**Step 3: Interest on 2nd deposit (1 July) for remaining 6 months:**

⇒ I₃ = 9920 × (3.9 ÷ 100) = ₹386.88

**Step 4: Total Interest Gained:**

⇒ Total Interest = I₁ (on 1st) + I₂ (on 1st) + I₃ (on 2nd)

⇒ Total Interest = 386.88 + 401.96832 + 386.88 = ₹1,175.72832

⇒ Rounding to two decimal places = ₹1,175.73

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,175.73.**

Half-Yearly Compounding Formula

When interest is compounded **half-yearly**, the formula becomes A = P[1 + (R/2)/100]²ⁿ, where R is the annual rate and n is the number of years.

questions.question: Which of the following national parks is recognised as the world's only floating national park?

options.text: Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Keibul Lamjao National Park is located in the state of **Manipur, India**, on Loktak Lake.
 
• It is **recognized as the world's only floating national park**, as it consists of large masses of floating vegetation known as "phumdis."
 
• The park is the **last natural habitat of the endangered Sangai deer**, also known as the dancing deer (Rucervus eldii eldii).
 
• Keibul Lamjao National Park was **declared a national park in 1977** to protect the unique ecosystem and its wildlife.
 
• The park covers an area of approximately **40 square kilometers**, and the phumdis play a critical role in supporting the ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phumdis:**

 
 
• Phumdis are floating masses of vegetation, soil, and organic matter at various stages of decomposition, unique to Loktak Lake.
 
• They serve as a critical habitat for wildlife and are an integral part of the ecological balance of Loktak Lake.
 
 
 
• **Sangai Deer:**
 
 
• The Sangai deer is an endangered species endemic to Manipur.
 
• It is culturally significant and is referred to as the state animal of Manipur.
 
• The deer’s unique gait, which resembles dancing, has earned it the nickname "dancing deer."
 
 
 
• **Loktak Lake:**
 
 
• Loktak Lake is the largest freshwater lake in northeast India and is known for its phumdis.
 
• The lake plays a crucial role in the livelihood of the local communities and provides water for hydropower generation, irrigation, and drinking purposes.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Efforts:**
 
 
• The Manipur Forest Department, along with other organizations, is actively working to conserve the habitat of the Sangai deer and the unique ecosystem of Keibul Lamjao National Park.
 
• Efforts include monitoring wildlife, reducing human interference, and raising awareness among local communities.

questions.question: If 14 : A :: A : 56, find the positive value of A.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When three numbers are in **continued proportion** (a : b :: b : c), the middle term is the **Mean Proportional**.

Direct formula: A = √(14 × 56)

⇒ A = √(14 × 14 × 4) = 14 × 2 = 28

**∴ The correct answer is 28.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio 14 : A is proportional to A : 56.

**Formula Used:** Product of **Extremes** = Product of **Means**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0d288c455a3db2a758c7c0003764ae6ce584da85cf3b48fa63cf37c53ced7906.png] 

⇒ 14 / A = A / 56

⇒ A² = 14 × 56

⇒ A² = 784

⇒ A = √784

⇒ A = 28

**∴ The correct answer is 28.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

If b is the mean proportional between a and c, then b = √(ac).

Third Proportional

In the proportion a : b :: b : c, the term c is called the third proportional and is calculated as c = b² / a.

Fourth Proportional

If a : b :: c : d, then d is the fourth proportional where d = (b × c) / a.</p

questions.question: Which of the following companies assisted the Raja of Cochin in expelling the Portuguese from his kingdom in 1663?

• In **1663**, the **Dutch East India Company **(Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie or VOC) assisted the** Raja of Cochin in ousting the Portuguese from his kingdom**.
 
• The Portuguese had established their presence in Cochin since the early 16th century, using it as a key port for trade in spices.
 
• The Dutch aimed to dominate the spice trade in the Malabar Coast and saw the Portuguese as their primary competitors.
 
• The** Dutch captured Cochin and other Portuguese territories in the region**, marking a significant shift in colonial power dynamics in South India.
 
• This event was part of a broader conflict between European colonial powers over control of trade routes and resources in Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The Portuguese were the first European colonial power to establish a stronghold in India, starting with Vasco da Gama's arrival in Calicut in 1498.
 
• Cochin was one of their earliest and most important bases, established in 1503.
 
• They controlled trade in spices like pepper, cardamom, and cinnamon from the Malabar Coast.
 
 
 
• **Dutch East India Company (VOC):**
 
 
• Founded in 1602, the VOC was a powerful trading corporation that sought to monopolize trade in the East Indies (modern-day Indonesia and surrounding areas).
 
• It played a significant role in colonial expansion in Asia, particularly in the spice trade.
 
• The VOC set up trading posts in various parts of India, including Surat, Nagapattinam, and Cochin.

• The 16th and 17th centuries saw intense rivalry between European powers like the Portuguese, Dutch, French, and British for control of trade in Asia.
 
• These conflicts often involved alliances with local rulers, as seen in the Dutch support for the Raja of Cochin.
 
• Such rivalries eventually led to the decline of Portuguese influence in India and the rise of Dutch and later British dominance.

• Cochin (modern-day Kochi, Kerala) was a major port city and trade hub on the Malabar Coast.
 
• It was strategically important for controlling the spice trade, which was highly lucrative in the European markets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dasharatha succeeded Emperor Ashoka** to the throne of the Maurya Empire in approximately **232 BCE**.
 
• He was the grandson of Ashoka and ruled the eastern part of the Mauryan Empire, including Magadha.
 
• Dasharatha is known for continuing Ashoka’s policy of spreading Buddhism and maintaining the empire's stability during his reign.
 
• Inscriptions such as the** Nagarjuni Hills cave inscriptions **suggest Dasharatha dedicated these caves to the **Ajivikas**, a sect patronized by Ashoka as well.
 
• Dasharatha’s reign marked the beginning of the decline of the Mauryan Empire, as it became fragmented after Ashoka's death.

• Ashoka was one of the greatest emperors in Indian history, known for his role in spreading Buddhism across Asia.
 
• His reign marked the peak of the Mauryan Empire's territorial expansion and administrative efficiency.
 
• The Edicts of Ashoka, inscribed on rocks and pillars, reflect his policies of Dhamma and social welfare.

• After Ashoka's death, the Mauryan Empire gradually weakened due to internal divisions and lack of strong leadership.
 
• The empire fragmented into smaller kingdoms, leading to the rise of regional powers such as the Shunga Dynasty.
 
 
 
• **Ajivikas Sect:**

questions.question: The least number which, when diminished by 9, is divisible by 13, 20, 10 and 23 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Required number = **LCM** of (13, 20, 10, 23) + 9

**LCM** (13, 20, 10, 23) = 13 × 23 × 20 = 299 × 20 = 5980

Required number = 5980 + 9 = 5989

**∴ The correct answer is 5989.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Divisors are 13, 20, 10, and 23. The number is **diminished by 9**.

**Formula:** Required Number = **LCM**(Divisors) + Remainder/Diminished value

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fa78e1166889a577b39de2893da443cda18585f1df2a850a9608db511338e860.png] 

⇒ Step 1: Find **LCM** of 13, 20, 10, 23

⇒ Factors of 10 = 2 × 5

⇒ Factors of 20 = 2² × 5

⇒ Prime factors of 13 = 13 (Prime)

⇒ Prime factors of 23 = 23 (Prime)

⇒ **LCM** = 2² × 5 × 13 × 23 = 4 × 5 × 299 = 20 × 299 = 5980

⇒ Step 2: According to the question, (Number − 9) = 5980

⇒ Number = 5980 + 9 = 5989

**∴ The correct answer is 5989.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM (Least Common Multiple)

The smallest positive integer that is **divisible** by each of the given numbers. For prime numbers, LCM is their product.

Divisibility Rule for Diminished Numbers

If a number x when diminished by k is divisible by a, b, c, then **x = LCM(a, b, c) + k**. Conversely, if increased by k, then **x = LCM(a, b, c) − k**.

Prime Numbers

Since 13 and 23 are **prime numbers**, they must be included in the multiplication for calculating the LCM.</p

questions.question: Saline and Alkaline soils are most commonly found in:

options.text: the Deltas of Ganga and Godavari

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**drought-prone areas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Saline and alkaline soils are commonly found in **regions with low rainfall and arid or semi-arid climatic conditions**, such as drought-prone areas.
 
• These soils develop due to the **accumulation of salts and lack of adequate leaching** caused by limited water availability.
 
• They are characterized by **high pH levels** (alkaline nature), poor fertility, and the presence of excessive sodium, calcium, and magnesium salts.
 
• Such soils are often seen in **parts of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana, Punjab, and Uttar Pradesh**, where drought conditions are frequent.
 
• Saline and alkaline soils pose challenges for agriculture, requiring **specialized soil treatments like gypsum application** and irrigation management.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Saline Soils:**

 
 
• Contain high levels of soluble salts such as sodium chloride and sodium sulfate.
 
• Have poor structure and water infiltration, negatively impacting plant growth.
 
• Crop cultivation requires techniques like leaching and salt-tolerant crops.
 
 
 
• **Alkaline Soils:**
 
 
• Characterized by high pH (greater than 8.5) due to excessive sodium carbonate.
 
• Typically found in areas with poor drainage and dry climates.
 
• Gypsum is often used to reduce alkalinity and improve soil structure.
 
 
 
• **Leaching Process:**
 
 
• Leaching involves flushing out salts from the soil using adequate water supply.
 
• This process is essential for reclaiming saline and alkaline soils.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Agriculture:**
 
 
• Saline and alkaline soils reduce crop yields due to poor nutrient availability.
 
• Farmers often use salt-tolerant crops like barley, cotton, and mustard for cultivation.
 
• Soil amendments like organic matter and gypsum help restore fertility.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the underlying data structure that forms the basis of an electronic spreadsheet like MS Excel?

A hierarchical tree structure organizing data into nodes and branches
A two-dimensional grid composed of rows and columns intersecting to form cells
A linear sequence of data entries, similar to a text document

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Electronic spreadsheets, such as MS Excel, are fundamentally based on a **two-dimensional grid structure**.
 
• Data is organized in **rows (horizontal) and columns (vertical)**, intersecting to form cells where information can be stored.
 
• Each cell in the grid can hold **text, numbers, formulas, or other data types** used for computation and analysis.

questions.question: A can complete a piece of work in 18 days and B can complete it in 22 days. If they work on alternate days, starting with B on the first day, then in how many days will the work be finished?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(18, 22) = 198 units.

Efficiency: A = 11, B = 9.

2-day cycle (B+A) = 9 + 11 = 20 units.

In 9 cycles (18 days), work done = 9 × 20 = 180 units. Remaining = 18 units.

Day 19: B does 9 units. Remaining = 9 units. Day 20: A does 9/11 of work.

Total time = 18 + 1 + 9/11 = 19 9/11 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 19 9/11 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A finishes in 18 days, B finishes in 22 days. They work **alternately** starting with **B**.

 
 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency** 
 A 18 198 11 
 B 22 9 

⇒ Work done in first 2 days (B then A) = 9 + 11 = 20 units.

⇒ Number of such 2-day cycles = 198 ÷ 20 = 9 cycles with remainder 18.

⇒ Days for 9 cycles = 9 × 2 = 18 days.

⇒ Remaining work = 198 − 180 = 18 units.

⇒ 19th day (B's turn): B completes 9 units. Remaining work = 18 − 9 = 9 units.

⇒ 20th day (A's turn): Time taken by A = 9 ÷ 11 days.

⇒ Total time = 18 + 1 + 9/11 = 19 9/11 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 19 9/11 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Alternate Day Work

In alternate day problems, always calculate the work done in one full cycle (e.g., 2 days if there are 2 people) and divide the total work by this cycle's efficiency.

Efficiency and Time

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time. If A takes T₁ days and B takes T₂ days, their efficiencies are in the ratio T₂ : T₁.</p

questions.question: Priya bought 45 kg of apples and mangoes for ₹1,240. The prices of apples and mangoes were ₹25/kg and ₹30/kg, respectively. How much money did she spend on mangoes separately?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Assume all **45 kg** are **apples**: Cost = 45 × 25 = ₹1125.

Difference from **total cost** = 1240 − 1125 = ₹115.

Difference in price per kg (**mangoes** − **apples**) = 30 − 25 = ₹5.

Weight of **mangoes** = 115 ÷ 5 = 23 kg.

Total money spent on **mangoes** = 23 × 30 = ₹690.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹690.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total weight of **apples** and **mangoes** = 45 kg, Total cost = ₹1,240. Price of **apples** = ₹25/kg, Price of **mangoes** = ₹30/kg.

**Formula Used:** Total Cost = (Weight₁ × Price₁) + (Weight₂ × Price₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0ca81239a7899d02ffb2180c073add1e615f76efe2676cceceda4400d72409da.png] 

Let the weight of **mangoes** be x kg.

⇒ Weight of **apples** = (45 − x) kg

⇒ 30 × x + 25 × (45 − x) = 1240

⇒ 30x + 1125 − 25x = 1240

⇒ 5x = 1240 − 1125

⇒ 5x = 115

⇒ x = 115 ÷ 5 = 23 kg

⇒ Money spent on **mangoes** = 23 × 30 = ₹690

**∴ The correct answer is ₹690.**

**__Additional Information__**

Alligation Rule

It is used to find the ratio in which two components at different prices are mixed to get a mixture at a mean price: Ratio = (Dearer Price − Mean Price) : (Mean Price − Cheaper Price).

questions.question: The Capital Adequacy Ratio, sometimes seen in news, is related to which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Banking operations**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR)** is a metric used to measure the **financial strength of banks**, ensuring they have enough capital to absorb potential losses.
 
• It is expressed as a percentage of a bank's risk-weighted credit exposures, calculated using Tier 1 and Tier 2 capital.
 
• CAR is mandated by international banking regulations such as the Basel Accords, which promote financial stability and reduce systemic risks.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) requires Indian banks to maintain a minimum CAR of 9%, higher than the Basel III global standard of 8%.
 
• The ratio ensures banks can sustain operations even during financial crises, safeguarding depositors' interests and maintaining trust in the banking system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Basel Accords:**

 
 
• International banking regulatory frameworks developed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision.
 
• Basel I (1988), Basel II (2004), and Basel III (2010) focus on improving risk management and enhancing financial stability.
 
• Basel III introduced stricter CAR requirements, liquidity coverage ratios, and leverage ratios.
 
 
 
• **Tier 1 and Tier 2 Capital:**
 
 
• Tier 1 capital consists of core capital like equity and disclosed reserves, which can absorb losses directly.
 
• Tier 2 capital includes supplementary capital such as subordinated debt and undisclosed reserves.
 
• Banks use both types of capital to calculate CAR, with Tier 1 being more critical for financial stability.
 
 
 
• **Risk-Weighted Assets (RWA):**
 
 
• Assets are assigned risk weights based on their inherent credit, market, and operational risks.
 
• For example, government securities may have a lower risk weight compared to loans to businesses.
 
• RWA calculations are crucial for determining CAR and compliance with regulatory standards.
 
 
 
• **Importance of CAR:**
 
 
• Maintains depositor confidence by ensuring banks are financially stable.
 
• Helps mitigate risks of insolvency during economic downturns.
 
• Promotes responsible lending and banking practices.

To create a cybersecurity curriculum for university students
To establish a national cybersecurity task force
To develop a mobile game promoting cybersecurity awareness

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To develop a mobile game promoting cybersecurity awareness**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'Trinetra' project by IIT Tirupati primarily focuses on **developing a mobile game designed to promote cybersecurity awareness**.
 
• This initiative aims to **educate users about cybersecurity threats** in an engaging and interactive manner.
 
• The project leverages **gamification techniques** to make learning about cybersecurity concepts more accessible and appealing.
 
• 'Trinetra' aligns with the growing need for awareness about cyber risks due to increasing digital dependence in daily activities.
 
• By targeting a wide audience, including students and professionals, the project seeks to **strengthen cybersecurity practices at the individual level**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cybersecurity Awareness:**

 
 
• Cybersecurity awareness involves understanding the risks associated with online activities and adopting safe practices to protect personal and organizational data.
 
• It is crucial in today's era of increasing cyber threats, such as phishing, malware, ransomware, and identity theft.
 
 
 
• **Gamification in Education:**
 
 
• Gamification refers to the use of game-like elements, such as points, badges, and levels, to make learning more engaging and effective.
 
• It has been widely adopted in various fields, including cybersecurity, to improve user engagement and retention of knowledge.
 
 
 
• **Cybersecurity Challenges:**
 
 
• India has witnessed a significant increase in cyber incidents, prompting the need for initiatives to enhance cybersecurity education and awareness.
 
• Projects like 'Trinetra' help bridge the gap between technical knowledge and public understanding of cyber risks.
 
 
 
• **National Cybersecurity Efforts:**
 
 
• The Indian government has launched various programs and frameworks to enhance cybersecurity infrastructure, such as the National Cyber Security Policy.
 
• Educational institutions like IITs actively contribute by developing innovative solutions, including awareness campaigns and technological tools.

questions.question: How can a foreigner who has lived in India for 12 years acquire Indian citizenship?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**By naturalisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Indian citizenship can be acquired by a foreigner who has resided in India for a continuous period of **12 years** under the provisions of the **Citizenship Act, 1955**.
 
• The process is known as **naturalisation**, which is detailed in Section 6 of the Citizenship Act, 1955.
 
• To be eligible, the individual must have resided in India for **11 years cumulatively** in the 14 years preceding the application and for **12 months continuously** before submitting the application.
 
• The applicant must also meet specific qualifications, such as **good character**, adequate knowledge of an Indian language, and renunciation of citizenship of the foreign country.
 
• Upon successful application, citizenship is granted by a certificate issued by the **Government of India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Citizenship Act, 1955:**

 
 
• The Citizenship Act, 1955, governs the acquisition, termination, and supplementary provisions of Indian citizenship.
 
• It provides five methods for acquiring citizenship: by birth, descent, registration, naturalisation, and incorporation of territory.
 
 
 
• **Naturalisation vs Registration:**
 
 
• Naturalisation is for foreigners who meet the residency and other criteria, while registration is for specific categories like persons of Indian origin (PIOs) or spouses of Indian citizens.
 
• Registration requires a shorter residency period compared to naturalisation.
 
 
 
• **Language Requirement:**
 
 
• The applicant must have adequate knowledge of at least one of the **official languages of India** as specified in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Renunciation of Previous Citizenship:**
 
 
• India does not allow dual citizenship; therefore, an individual must renounce their previous citizenship to acquire Indian citizenship via naturalisation.
 
 
 
• **Good Character Criterion:**
 
 
• The applicant must demonstrate good moral character, verified through background checks during the application process.

questions.question: The Palk Strait is an inlet of which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bay of Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Palk Strait is a narrow stretch of water that lies between **India and Sri Lanka**.
 
• It connects the **Bay of Bengal to the northeast** and the **Palk Bay to the southwest**.
 
• The strait is named after Sir Robert Palk, a Governor of Madras during British rule in India.
 
• The Palk Strait is characterized by shallow waters and a chain of low islands and reef shoals collectively known as **Adam's Bridge or Rama's Bridge**.
 
• This geographical feature has been historically significant for trade and cultural exchanges between India and Sri Lanka.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bay of Bengal:**

 
 
• The Bay of Bengal is the largest bay in the world and is bordered by India, Bangladesh, Myanmar, and Sri Lanka.
 
• Major rivers like the Ganges, Brahmaputra, Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri drain into this bay.
 
• It plays a vital role in monsoon dynamics and is home to important marine biodiversity.
 
• The bay is a hub for international shipping and fishing industries.
 
 
 
• **Adam's Bridge:**
 
 
• Also known as Rama's Bridge, it is a chain of limestone shoals connecting Pamban Island (India) to Mannar Island (Sri Lanka).
 
• It is mentioned in ancient Hindu texts, including the Ramayana.
 
• Geological studies suggest the feature may have formed due to tectonic activity and sediment deposition.
 
 
 
• **Geopolitical Importance of the Palk Strait:**
 
 
• The strait serves as a maritime boundary between India and Sri Lanka.
 
• It is significant for fisheries and marine trade in the region.
 
• India and Sri Lanka cooperate on managing maritime security and combating illegal fishing in the strait.
 
 
 
• **Marine Biodiversity:**
 
 
• The Palk Strait is home to diverse marine species, including corals, fish, and crustaceans.
 
• Efforts are underway to conserve the fragile marine ecosystem in the region.

questions.question: What does setting a Page Break in MS Excel 365 allow you to control?

options.text: Whether formulas are recalculated before printing
Where headers appear on each page
The maximum size of printable margins
Where the worksheet splits across printed pages

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Where the worksheet splits across printed pages**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Setting a Page Break in MS Excel allows users to control **where the worksheet content is divided across pages during printing.**
 
• Page Breaks can be manually inserted in Excel using **“Page Layout” → “Breaks” → “Insert Page Break”**.
 
• This feature is helpful for ensuring that specific sections or rows are printed together, avoiding incomplete data splits across pages.
 
• Excel supports both **horizontal and vertical page breaks**, providing flexibility in organizing printed outputs.
 
• Page Break Preview mode allows users to visually adjust and review page breaks before printing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Page Setup Options:**

 
 
• Excel allows users to customize margins, orientation (portrait or landscape), and paper size under the “Page Setup” menu.
 
• These settings directly influence how the printed worksheet appears.
 
 
 
• **Print Area:**
 
 
• Users can define a specific print area to ensure only selected portions of the worksheet are printed.
 
• This is useful for focusing on relevant data while excluding unnecessary information from printouts.
 
 
 
• **Headers and Footers:**
 
 
• Excel allows customization of headers and footers to include page numbers, dates, or custom text on printed pages.
 
• This feature improves document organization and presentation.
 
 
 
• **Print Preview:**
 
 
• Print Preview helps users inspect the layout and formatting of the worksheet before printing.
 
• This ensures alignment and avoids printing errors or unnecessary page breaks.
 
 
 
• **Automatic Page Breaks:**
 
 
• Excel automatically inserts page breaks based on paper size and margins if manual page breaks are not defined.
 
• Users can override these automatic breaks by inserting custom ones.
